summary:
MARSNAV – Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

MARSNAV is an interactive web-based Martian exploration and survival mapping system designed to support future human missions to Mars. We developed a digital map application that uses scientific data from NASA and other planetary missions to help users explore Martian terrain and identify important locations.

The platform provides interactive map layers displaying rover landing sites, geological features, surface hazards, underground water ice resources, and potential natural shelters. It also includes a Mars route planner that allows users to create exploration routes, calculate travel distances and estimated durations, estimate oxygen consumption, and evaluate route safety based on terrain, hazards, and available imagery.

MARSNAV addresses the challenge of understanding and navigating the dangerous Martian environment by bringing essential exploration and safety information into one platform. It is important because it demonstrates how scientific data and geospatial technology can support safer mission planning, resource identification, and future human exploration of Mars.
details:
MARSNAV: An Interplanetary Survival Guide : Martian Map

MARSNAV is an interactive web based Mars exploration platform developed by my Team Useless for the NASA SPACE APPS Challenge 2026.Our project aims to make Mars exploration easier by bringing Martian maps, Scientific information, Surface Hazards and route planning features in one application.

A User can explore the surface of Mars through our interactive map and Discover important locations such as Jezero crater, gale crater, Olympus mons etc.

Our Application also includes a Mars walk route planner, where one user can create exploration routes by adding and arranging way points. It calculates travel distance and oxygen consumption.

The main benefit of our project is that it makes different types of Martian exploration information easier to access and understand. It can helps students , researchers visualize the challenges involved in exploring Mars.

We developed the project using HTML5, CSS3 and JAVASCRIPT. Leaflet.js is used for interactive mapping, Chart.js for data visualization and Font Awesome for interface Icons. We also incorporated planetary Map services and scientific resources from NASA Mars Trek, USGS astrogeology and open planetary.

what makes MARSNAV creative?

We combine planetary exploration, route planning, resource estimation and hazard assessment into a single interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying a map of Mars, we wanted users to interact with the terrain and experience some of the decisions involved in planning a hypothetical surface exploration mission.

During development, we considered terrain conditions, potential surface hazards, travel distance, crew size, estimated oxygen requirements and the availability of scientific imagery. We also considered making the interface easy to understand and use.
